`ECHO_BACKEND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`:

```md
# Echo Backend Integration - Implementation Summary

## Overview

This document describes the complete implementation of Echo Backend features for the echo-reverse project, following the specifications from:
- [Echo Backend Angel Documentation](https://echo-23.gitbook.io/angel)
- [LLMs Full Text](https://echo-23.gitbook.io/angel/llms-full.txt)

All features maintain the original UI/UX/layout from Reverse Slap / Reverse Slop.

## File Structure

### AngelScript Files (`/app/echo/`)

#### 1. `echo-backend-extensions.as`
Complete Echo Backend API wrappers including:
- **Rendering**: World-to-screen conversions, viewport size, FPS monitoring, camera info
- **Mathematics**: Matrix/quaternion operations, geometry utilities, easing functions, Perlin noise
- **Process**: Module/process management, memory reading, signature scanning
- **Unreal Engine**: W2S, bone reading, entity scanning
- **Unity Engine**: W2S, transform position, prefab ID lookup, entity scanning
- **Source Engine**: W2S, entity access, health reading
- **Source 2 Engine**: W2S, controller/pawn access
- **Tracing**: Ray casting, line tracing, bbox clipping
- **Clipping**: Point clipping, on-screen detection
- **Hashing**: FNV-1a, CRC32, MD5, SHA256
- **System**: System info, process info, module list

#### 2. `echo-networking.as`
HTTP/WebSocket client implementations:
- HTTP GET, POST, PUT, DELETE with headers and timeout
- WebSocket connect, send, close, message handling
- Configuration management
- Entity caching
- Logging and notifications

#### 3. `echo-rpc-extensions.as`
RPC message handlers for all Echo Backend features:
- Mathematics handlers (angle calculation, matrix operations, etc.)
- SIMD vector operations
- Memory operations (read buffer, batch read, pattern scanning)
- Rendering handlers
- Engine-specific handlers (Unreal, Unity, Source, Source 2)
- Tracing and clipping handlers
- Utility handlers (hashing, system info)
- Performance monitoring handlers
- Value tracking handlers
- Collections handlers (array, map operations)
- Networking handlers (HTTP, WebSocket)

#### 4. `echo-math-utilities.as`
Advanced mathematics utilities:
- Matrix4x4 class with full operations
- Quaternion class with full operations
- Vec2, Vec3, Vec4 classes
- Ray, Plane, Bbox classes
- Ray-plane intersection
- Ray-box intersection
- Point-in-polygon
- Perlin noise 1D/2D/3D
- Easing functions (linear, quad, cubic, etc.)
- Rotation utilities
- Geometry utilities

#### 5. `echo-advanced-scanner.as`
Advanced memory scanning capabilities:
- Pattern scanning (single and multi-pattern)
- Value scanning
- Entity scanning (Unreal, Unity)
- Pointer chain scanning
- Memory dumping (regions, modules)
- Signature database
- Value tracking
- Memory change detection
- Region analysis
- RTTI detection
- Pool allocator detection

#### 6. `echo-performance.as`
Performance monitoring utilities:
- Performance counter manager
- FPS monitoring
- Frame time analysis
- GPU profiling
- Memory usage monitoring
- CPU usage monitoring
- Thread monitoring
- Performance graphs
- Main performance monitor class

#### 7. `echo-rpc-handlers.as`
RPC handler registry and routing:
- Handler registration system
- Type definitions for RPC messages
- Helper functions for address parsing
- Main router for extended RPC calls

### TypeScript Files (`/app/src/lib/`)

#### `echo-extensions.ts`
Complete TypeScript client API for all Echo Backend features:

**Exported Modules:**
- `unreal` - Unreal Engine functions
- `unity` - Unity Engine functions
- `source` - Source Engine functions
- `source2` - Source 2 Engine functions
- `memory` - Memory operations
- `rendering` - Rendering utilities
- `math` - Mathematics utilities
- `tracing` - Tracing functions
- `clipping` - Clipping functions
- `performance` - Performance monitoring
- `valueTracking` - Value tracking utilities
- `networking` - HTTP and WebSocket clients
- `collections` - Dynamic array and map operations
- `simd` - SIMD vector operations
- `util` - Utility functions (hashing, system info, etc.)

**Exported Types:**
- Vec2, Vec3, Vec4, Bbox2D
- FpsInfo, W2SResult, BoneInfo
- PatternScanResult, ValueScanResult, EntityInfo
- MemoryDump, PerformanceCounter, MemoryUsageInfo
- CpuUsageInfo, ThreadInfo, MemoryRegionInfo
- TrackedValue, PerformanceGraphPoint, PerformanceSummary
- Matrix4x4, Quaternion, Ray, Plane
- HttpRequestOptions, HttpResponse, WebSocketMessage
- ClipResult, HashResult

**Exported Functions:**
- `toHex`, `parseHex`, `parseAddress`
- `detectGameEngine`

### React Components (`/app/src/components/panels/`)

#### 1. `AdvancedMemoryScannerPanel.tsx`
Advanced memory scanning interface with:
- Pattern scanning (single module or all modules)
- Value scanning with type selection
- Signature database management
- Multi-pattern scanning
- Results display with filtering
- Module browser

Features:
- Auto-refresh with configurable interval
- Results truncation for large scans
- Pattern validation
- Hex/decimal address input
- Module selection from loaded modules

#### 2. `PerformanceMonitorPanel.tsx`
Comprehensive performance monitoring dashboard:
- Real-time FPS monitoring
- Frame time analysis
- Memory usage tracking
- CPU usage tracking
- Thread monitoring
- Performance graphs (FPS, Memory, CPU)
- Counter management

Features:
- Multiple tabs: Overview, Counters, Memory, CPU, Threads
- Auto-refresh with configurable interval
- Performance counter display with min/max/avg
- Memory and CPU usage percentages
- Thread list with status
- Interactive graphs with history

#### 3. `ValueTrackerPanel.tsx`
Value tracking and monitoring:
- Track any memory address
- Automatic value change detection
- History of value changes
- Multiple value types support

Features:
- Two tabs: Tracker and History
- Address input with module browser
- Value name labeling
- Change highlighting
- History of all value changes with timestamps
- Delta calculation for numeric values

## Activity Rail Integration

Added three new panel entries to the ActivityRail:

1. **Memory Scanner** (Search icon)
   - ID: `memory_scanner`
   - Component: `AdvancedMemoryScannerPanel`

2. **Performance Monitor** (Activity icon)
   - ID: `performance`
   - Component: `PerformanceMonitorPanel`

3. **Value Tracker** (Eye icon)
   - ID: `value_tracker`
   - Component: `ValueTrackerPanel`

## RPC Message Types

All Echo Backend features are exposed via RPC messages. The complete list includes:

### Mathematics
- `calculate_angle`
- `calculate_2d_bbox`
- `matrix_multiply`
- `matrix_vector_multiply`
- `quaternion_multiply`
- `ray_plane_intersection`
- `perlin_noise`
- `ease_in_out_quad`

## Usage Examples

### TypeScript (Frontend)

```typescript
import { memory, math, rendering, unreal, performance } from '@/lib/echo-extensions';

// Pattern scanning
const result = await memory.patternScanModule('game.dll', '48 8B 05 ?? ?? ?? ??', 'x??x???');
if (result.success) {
  console.log('Found patterns:', result.results);
}

// World-to-screen
const screenPos = await unreal.w2s({ x: 100, y: 200, z: 50 });
if (screenPos.success) {
  console.log('Screen position:', screenPos.x, screenPos.y);
}

// Angle calculation
const angle = await math.calculateAngle({ x: 0, y: 0, z: 0 }, { x: 10, y: 5, z: 2 });
console.log('Angle:', angle.pitch, angle.yaw);

// Performance monitoring
const summary = await performance.getSummary();
console.log('FPS:', summary.fps);

// Memory usage
const memoryInfo = await performance.getMemoryUsage();
console.log('Memory usage:', memoryInfo.memory?.physicalUsagePercent, '%');
```

### AngelScript (Backend)

```angelscript
// Pattern scanning
array<PatternScanResult@> results = pattern_scan_module("game.dll", "48 8B 05 ?? ?? ?? ??", "x??x???");
for (uint i = 0; i < results.length(); i++) {
    print("Found at: " + to_hex_string(results[i].address));
}

// World-to-screen
Vec3 world_pos = Vec3(100, 200, 50);
Vec2 screen_pos;
if (unreal::world_to_screen(world_pos, screen_pos)) {
    print("Screen position: (" + screen_pos.x + ", " + screen_pos.y + ")");
}

// Matrix operations
Matrix4x4 a, b, result;
a = Matrix4x4::identity();
b = Matrix4x4::identity();
result = a * b;

// Performance monitoring
g_performance_monitor.update();
map<string, string> summary = g_performance_monitor.get_summary();
print("FPS: " + summary["fps"]);

// Memory usage
MemoryUsageInfo info = g_memory_monitor.get_last_info();
print("Memory usage: " + info.physical_usage_percent + "%");
```

- Existing echo-reverse libraries and components

## Performance Considerations

1. **Lazy Loading**: All new panels are lazy-loaded to keep initial bundle small
2. **Auto-Refresh**: Configurable refresh intervals for performance monitoring
3. **Result Limiting**: Large scan results are truncated to prevent UI lag
4. **Efficient Updates**: Only changed values trigger UI updates

---

echo-reverse brings live analysis, memory tooling, game-engine inspection and
AngelScript development together in a Windows desktop app. Echo owns the target
attachment and provides the memory and disassembly primitives; AngelScript
agents connect those primitives to the workbench over a local WebSocket relay.
The existing reverse-slop layout remains at the center of the experience.

| Explore | Build | Automate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Disassemble functions, browse PE metadata, inspect strings and follow cross-references. | Scan and watch memory, emulate functions, design overlays and work with AngelScript. | Connect MCP clients, export engine data and prepare handoffs for external analysis tools. |

## Requirements

| Requirement | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Platform | Windows 10/11 x64 and Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime |
| Backend | [Echo](https://echo-23.gitbook.io/angel), with a target attached |
| Source builds | Node.js 20+, Rust and MSVC build tools |

The workbench relies on Echo for target access. Echo is distributed separately.

### Automatic releases

Each successful, current `main` build advances the patch version in the npm,
Tauri and Cargo manifests and lockfiles, commits that change, and creates a
matching `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` tag. The workflow starts a build for the tag;
after tests and signature verification, it publishes the Windows portable
executable, NSIS installer, Debian package and updater manifest. A newer push
to `main` supersedes an older build before tagging.

Actions must be allowed to write contents and dispatch workflows, and branch
protection must permit the Actions bot to push the version commit. Configure
`TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` to match the updater public key,
`TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` if needed, and `ECHO_APT_SIGNING_KEY` for
the separate APT repository job. If dispatch fails after the tag is pushed,
manually run the `build` workflow with that tag selected. Automatic releases
increment the patch; synchronize the source versions before merging to change
the major or minor version. Linux is a UI preview; Echo runs on Windows.

## Quick start

1. Install the desktop app from a [release](https://github.com/NetVar1337/echo-reverse/releases) (`echo-reverse_*_x64-setup.exe`, or the portable `echo-reverse.exe`), or [build it from source](#build-from-source). On startup it copies missing stock scripts to `%APPDATA%\scripts`. Installed builds check for updates on start, download them in the background and offer **Restart to update** in the status bar; **Settings → Updates** checks on demand.
2. Attach the target in Echo.
3. Load `echo-reverse.as` from Echo's script menu. Reopen the menu if the script is not listed. If the app started after the script, press **Connect** on the script's Echo tab.
4. Check the status bar for **Engine: Connected** and **Memory: Ready**. Open **Settings → Echo Relay** for connection diagnostics.
5. Optional: connect an MCP client to `http://127.0.0.1:9000/mcp`. For example:

   ```bash
   claude mcp add --transport http echo-reverse http://127.0.0.1:9000/mcp
   ```

6. Optional: configure an entity layout in **Overlay (ESP)**, install the generated script, then load `echo-reverse-overlay.as` in Echo.

Existing stock scripts are preserved on startup. To update an installed script,
install the current version explicitly from the Scripts panel; changed files are
backed up. Echo loads the script from its own menu.

The updater checks signed releases at startup, every six hours, when connectivity
returns, and on demand. Stable builds use the stable feed; preview builds use a
separate feed with a new build number for each successful main-branch build.
After download, choose **Restart to update**. On Windows the installer takes
over and restarts the installed app; on Linux the package installation may ask
for administrator credentials before restarting. A standalone Windows executable
uses the installer for updates, which installs a separate copy rather than
replacing the standalone file. Older preview builds that only know the stable
feed need one manual installation of a newer preview before automatic preview
updates become available.

### Terminal updates

On Debian or Ubuntu (amd64), add the signed APT repository once:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NetVar1337/echo-reverse/apt/repository-key.asc |
  gpg --dearmor | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/echo-reverse.gpg >/dev/null
echo 'deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/echo-reverse.gpg] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NetVar1337/echo-reverse/apt ./' |
  sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/echo-reverse.list >/dev/null
sudo apt update
sudo apt install echo-reverse
```

The signing key fingerprint is `C090 CFDF C459 CE89 1CC1 037C 6142 5CD2 86D4 000A`.
After setup, `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade` includes echo-reverse.
The APT repository contains stable releases; preview updates use the in-app
updater instead. The Linux build is a UI preview because
Echo itself runs on Windows.

To use `echo update` in Bash or Zsh, download the shell integration and source it
from your shell profile (for example, `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`):

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.config/echo-reverse
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NetVar1337/echo-reverse/main/packaging/shell/echo-update.sh -o ~/.config/echo-reverse/echo-update.sh
printf '\nsource ~/.config/echo-reverse/echo-update.sh\n' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.config/echo-reverse/echo-update.sh
```

In PowerShell, download the integration and dot-source it in your PowerShell
profile, then restart PowerShell:

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force (Split-Path $PROFILE) | Out-Null
$integration = Join-Path (Split-Path $PROFILE) 'echo-reverse-update.ps1'
Invoke-WebRequest 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NetVar1337/echo-reverse/main/packaging/shell/echo-update.ps1' -OutFile $integration
Add-Content $PROFILE "`n. '$integration'"
. $integration
```

On Windows, `echo update` opens the app, checks for a signed release, and starts
its installer if an update is available. Set `ECHO_REVERSE_EXE` to the executable
path if it is not installed in the default location. The command is available in
PowerShell; Windows Command Prompt has a built-in `echo` that cannot be overridden
by an executable. These shell integrations reserve exactly `echo update`; use
`builtin echo update` in Bash/Zsh or `Write-Output update` in PowerShell to print
that text. Other `echo` calls retain their usual behavior.

## Architecture and relay

Echo connects out to the relay; the desktop app hosts the relay on loopback and
routes requests to the appropriate agent lane. The UI analyzes Echo's attached
main module directly, including its PE structures and live memory.

```text
 Echo + attached target                   echo-reverse desktop
 ┌──────────────────────────┐            ┌──────────────────────────────┐
 │ echo-reverse.as          │── /agent ─▶│                              │
 │                          │── /agent-ext ▶  Relay 127.0.0.1:9000    │
 │ angel-menu-control.as    │── /agent-ui ▶│                              │
 └──────────────────────────┘            │  /agent-app ◀── Workspace   │
                                         └──────────┬──────────┬────────┘
                                               POST /rpc   POST /mcp
                                                   │           │
                                              UI / browser  MCP client
```

The relay is implemented in [`app/src-tauri/src/relay.rs`](app/src-tauri/src/relay.rs).
Its default port is `9000`; set `ECHO_RELAY_PORT` before launching the desktop
app to change it. The UI's relay URL is configurable in **Settings → Echo Relay**
and stored in local storage. If the port is already occupied, the app starts and
can use a compatible existing relay.

| Endpoint | Connection | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ws /agent` | Echo's native socket | Reads, module information, signatures, RTTI and disassembly |
| `ws /agent-ext` | `echo-reverse.as` | Attach/detach, writes, regions, loaded-module PE tables, raw/native scans, emulation and capabilities |
| `ws /agent-ui` | `angel-menu-control.as` | Overlay menu controls |
| `ws /agent-app` | Desktop workspace | Registers and executes app tools |
| `POST /rpc` | UI or compatible browser client | Routes an Echo request and returns its reply |
| `POST /mcp` | MCP client | JSON-RPC tools for agent workflows |
| `GET /status` | Local client | Reports relay lane state and diagnostics |

Settings probes the relay, Echo ping and extension capabilities. The built-in
relay tracks lane generations, pending requests, latency and errors, with a
limit of 128 pending requests per lane. Its `Host` and browser `Origin` checks
restrict access; request bodies are limited to 1 MiB. Requests time out after
60 seconds, or 900 seconds for app tools. `GET /mcp` returns `405`; the endpoint
uses JSON responses rather than an SSE stream.

## The workspace

| Area | What you'll find |
| --- | --- |
| Activity rail | Targets, Modules, Scripts, Unreal, Unity (IL2CPP), Source 2, Signature Doctor, RTTI, Data Types, Overlay, Menu Control, Deobfuscation and Settings |
| Workspace | Disassembly, Analysis, Strings, Memory, Emulator and PE Browser tabs |
| Status bar | Target and PID, Echo core/extension/menu lane state, image state, theme, update, Scripts and Settings shortcuts |

## Agent scripts

The relay scripts and the overlay template live in [`app/echo/`](app/echo). The
app installs missing relay scripts on start without replacing existing files, and the Scripts panel (`full`,
`read-only`) opens them with the process name substituted. They use documented
Echo APIs only.

- [`echo-reverse.as`](app/echo/echo-reverse.as) — the one script to load. It
  opens Echo's built-in socket on `/agent` and serves `attach` / `detach`,
  `write`, `regions`, loaded-module PE tables, raw/grouped scans, the native
  value scanner and `emulate` on `/agent-ext` through `ws::`. The emulator is
  driven by `uc::create_process`, so pages fault in from the target read-only
  and the game itself is never executed or touched.
- [`echo-reverse-agent.as`](app/echo/echo-reverse-agent.as) — read-only
  alternative: Echo's socket only, no writes, scans or emulator.
- [`echo-reverse-overlay.as`](app/echo/echo-reverse-overlay.as) — the ESP
  template. The Overlay panel rewrites its constants and installs it; it is not
  a relay script.
- [`templates/`](app/echo/templates) — the game templates from
  [echo-ai-toolkit](https://github.com/NetVar1337/echo-ai-toolkit) (MIT): basic,
  memory, menu, render, radar, aimbot, misc, loot, esp-bones, esp-preview,
  fortnite, valorant, ue5-sdk, unity-il2cpp and web-mv. The esp-preview
  template now bundles the complete upstream preview/layout implementation.
  The Scripts panel's
  `templates…` picker opens one with its target exe swapped for the attached
  process; `script_template` gives agents the same.

Echo loads scripts from `%APPDATA%\scripts`. Explicit installation backs up a
changed existing script as `.as.bak.N` before replacing it. Since startup
preserves existing stock scripts, update them explicitly when changing app
versions. Load the installed script from Echo's menu; `script_list` reports the
scripts available on disk.

## What you get

From a single attached target, move between live analysis, script development
and export workflows. Choose an area below for details and current limitations:

| Workflow | Capabilities |
| --- | --- |
| [Code and image analysis](#disassembly) | Disassembly, control flow, cross-references, strings and PE metadata |
| [Memory](#memory-and-the-scanner) | Hex editing, reusable typed structures, snapshots, scanning and watches |
| [Emulation](#emulator) | Register setup, traces, import stubs and emulator-only mappings |
| [Engine analysis](#unreal-dumper-7-style) | Unreal, Unity IL2CPP and Source 2 exploration and exports |
| [Signatures and RTTI](#signature-doctor-and-rtti) | Signature validation, catalogs, baselines and class names |
| [AngelScript](#scripts) | Editing, diagnostics, includes, bundling and installation |
| [Overlay](#overlay-esp) | Preview and generate an Echo ESP script |
| [Menu Control](#menu-control) | Read and drive an overlay's documented menu-control lane |
| [External tools](#deobfuscation-and-handoff) | Triage, dumps and handoff artifacts for static analysis |

### Disassembly

Functions from the module's exception directory, named from exports and your own
renames, listed with Zydis and with call/jump targets resolved to names.
Cross-references come from `xrefs_to`: rel32 branches, rip-relative loads
confirmed against the disassembly, and stored pointers in data sections
(vtables, tables), each with its containing function. The **Analysis** tab adds
a control-flow diagram, direct-call sites, function-size statistics and regular
expression search over the selected function's instruction operands.
Click an instruction to inspect its structured Zydis operands, including action,
registers, displacement and RIP-relative address. This needs the current full
extension script.

### Strings and PE Browser

ASCII and UTF-16 strings are extracted from the data sections of live memory
(cached per image, 64 MiB budget, 10k default limit, optional executable
sections). URL, path, command and RTTI/class-name filters are available, regular
expressions can be enabled, filtered rows export to CSV/JSON/TXT, and any
string can jump straight to its address in Memory. The PE Browser shows headers,
sections, imports, exports and the resource tree for the main image and every
other loaded module; the latter are read by the Echo extension's PE-table verbs,
so a DLL can be inspected without copying it out first.

### Memory and the scanner

Hex editor over live memory, 16 bytes a row, with a region list on the left and
in-place editing. **Pointers / struct** resolves an editable pointer chain and
reads named fields of integer, floating-point and pointer types. Base addresses
and offsets are hexadecimal; all offsets except the final field offset are
dereferenced. The **Data Types** rail stores reusable nested structs and enums,
imports/exports them as JSON, renders a packed C++ header, and applies a
selected layout to the current Memory address. The memory view can snapshot the current page and highlight
differences after a fresh read. It retains one snapshot in the view, with its
target and capture time. Live memory reads are not atomic.
**Pointers / struct** also saves named snapshots of up to 1 MiB in local storage,
compares matching ranges, filters changed bytes and exports differences. Its
bounded pointer search scans a contiguous readable range (up to 4 MiB); candidate
chains can be revalidated and module-relative bases survive relocation. Searches
are capped and may miss unaligned pointers or results beyond the cap.

The scanner supports a first pass (`exact`/`unknown`) followed by narrowing
(`exact`, `between`, `bigger`, `smaller`, `increased`, `decreased`, `changed`,
`unchanged`) across i8…f64. Each scan session retains its own results. Scans use
bounded Echo read batches, report byte or hit progress, and can be cancelled;
cancelling a refinement keeps its last completed results. First scans accept
hexadecimal start and exclusive end addresses, protection filters and hit/byte
limits. The header identifies capped results and omitted display rows, while
failed reads are reported. Signed and unsigned 64-bit values stay exact through
scanning and watch display, editing and freezing. A default first scan includes
present writable, non-executable regions; other protection filters are available.

The watchlist polls at 4 Hz, writes values back, and re-writes frozen entries
whenever the target changes them. Target or agent changes clear target-specific
results and watches; re-add a watch to freeze it on a new target. This is
checked by periodic polling, so a target change cannot be detected instantly.
Agents can run separate scans via `value_scan_session`, `value_scan_status` and
`value_scan_cancel`; the older raw extension `value_scan` interface remains
available. The extension provides the region list and the native socket provides
memory reads.
Scan presets are saved locally; session comparison and module grouping in the UI
use displayed hits and report when the results are partial.

### Emulator

Runs a function under Unicorn over the target's memory without touching the
game: initial registers in, registers and a bounded trace out. Calls that leave
the module are stubbed and logged with `rcx`/`rdx`/`r8`/`r9` and their
`module!export` name; memory stores are logged with the value written. Needs the
ext agent. The trace can be filtered by address, and registers that differ from
the previous run are highlighted. **Options** stores local presets and accepts
named emulator-only memory mappings as `name address size permissions [hexbytes]`
per line. Addresses and sizes are hexadecimal and page-aligned; permissions use
`r`, `w`, and `x`. Mappings need the current full extension script. Reinstall it
from Scripts and reload it in Echo after upgrading.
Results also show XMM/YMM values as byte-order hex, a bounded emulator memory
map and named fault types when the updated extension supplies them.

### Modules and dumps

The **Runtime captures** rail captures a live range of up to 16 MiB as JSON.
Unreadable pages remain explicit gaps; captures are not atomic. Open a saved
capture without an Echo target to inspect bytes and extract ASCII strings, or
open a second capture of the same range to compare changed and unavailable
bytes. The connection screen offers an offline entry point when no relay is
available. It can also open PE files up to 16 MiB of image space, map their
file-backed sections at a chosen load base, and show RVA and file offsets.
Loader relocations are not applied; comparison against live memory can therefore
include expected loader changes. Windows minidump memory-list and memory64-list
streams can be opened by selecting an individual captured range (up to 16 MiB;
the minidump file limit is 128 MiB). The capture view can disassemble up to
4 KiB of readable x86 or x64 bytes offline using iced-x86; it stops at 1,000
instructions and refuses ranges containing gaps.

Lists Echo's loaded modules, browses each module's live PE tables and dumps any
of them as a PE file: raw layout equals virtual layout and `ImageBase` is the
live base, so addresses match the process
and Ghidra, IDA, radare2,
[NoVmp](https://github.com/can1357/NoVmp) or
[Triton](https://github.com/JonathanSalwan/Triton) load it without relocating.
In memory the IAT holds resolved pointers and protected games wipe the import
directory, so the dump resolves every slot against the exports of the loaded
modules, appends a new import section and writes the name thunks back —
Scylla-style, but without a separate tool. Forwarded exports are named after the
module that implements them; ordinal-only imports are skipped.

Dumps land in `%APPDATA%\echo-reverse\out`.
Module captures compare imports, exports, sections, sampled ASCII strings and
the first 16 bytes of up to 256 functions. String reads are limited to 1 MiB
and 2,000 strings; capture warnings identify unavailable or truncated data.

### Unreal (Dumper-7 style)

Finds `GObjects` and the `FNamePool` by layout, detects the
`UStruct`/`FField`/`FProperty`/`UEnum`/`UFunction` offsets from objects every
game has the way [Dumper-7](https://github.com/Encryqed/Dumper-7)'s offset finder
does, then browses objects, dumps a class, struct or enum with member offsets and
sizes, functions with parameters and native exec addresses, and exports the whole
thing as one SDK header.

UE5 and UE4.25+ (FNamePool, chunked GObjects, FField properties) and older UE4
(TNameEntryArray, flat GObjects, UProperty objects) are covered. GObjects and GNames RVAs can be overridden independently, with discovery used for the other value. Known gaps: no
`TPair<FName, uint8>` enums (pre-4.15) and no 32-bit games.

Valorant builds hide `GObjects` behind a 7-state rotating cipher
([Dumper-7-VGK](https://github.com/sinistercodes/Dumper-7-VGK)). The panel scans
executable sections for the accessor's `0x2545F4914F6CDD1D` magic, walks back to
the RIP-relative `lea` that names the state struct, decrypts the pointer, and
only accepts it after the `FChunkedFixedUObjectArray` counts and the first
`FUObjectItem` validate. Both state layouts (`+0x40`/`+0x78` and `+0x00`/`+0x38`)
are tried; a successful result is marked `valorant` in `unreal_index` and in the
panel. Nothing is written to the game.

### Overlay (ESP)

The Overlay panel is [echo-esp-preview](https://github.com/speedsunderscore/echo-esp-preview)'s
idea wired to Echo's renderer. Configure the entity list RVA (directly or as a
pointer), count and stride, position/health/team offsets, the local team to
skip, the view-matrix RVA, Unity or Unreal coordinates, and the box size; the
stage previews the box, label and health bar arrangement.

Label and bar placement can be changed with the preview controls or by dragging and the configuration is saved locally.
The output is a complete AngelScript file, not an app-side renderer. It reads
entities with `process::read_uint64`, projects boxes with
`render::calculate_2d_bbox` (or `calculate_2d_bbox_unity`), and draws with
`render::draw_box` / `draw_text_outlined`; the checkboxes and colour pickers use
`ui::` and persist through `ui::config_path("echo-reverse-overlay")`. The panel
runs the generated file through the same Echo API checker as the Scripts panel
before it installs `echo-reverse-overlay.as` into `%APPDATA%\scripts`. Load it
from Echo's script menu like any other script. Swap the read block for your
game's real entity layout; the defaults are deliberately inert.

### Menu Control

The **Menu Control** rail is the in-app equivalent of
[angel-menu-mcp](https://github.com/Jozkah/angel-menu-mcp). It uses the same
`ui_list` / `ui_get` / `ui_set` frames over `ws://127.0.0.1:9000/agent-ui`,
groups controls by the overlay's own tab/category metadata, and can toggle
checkboxes, move sliders and select combo-box entries. Controls marked as
dangerous still require the overlay's live human **ARM** action; the app never
bypasses that gate.

The reusable lane core is bundled at
[`app/echo/integrations/angel-menu-control.as`](app/echo/integrations/angel-menu-control.as).
`app/scripts/generate-menu-registry.mjs` scans an overlay script and emits the
`amc_build_registry()` function for its controls. See the upstream
[integration guide](https://github.com/Jozkah/angel-menu-mcp/blob/main/INTEGRATION.md)
for the four hook points in the target script.

### Deobfuscation and handoff

The Deobf panel does the part a live process can do for the static
deobfuscation toolchain, and nothing that belongs to it:

- **Triage.** Samples up to three 64 KiB windows of every section for Shannon
  entropy, and flags W+X sections, packer-style section names (`.vmp*`,
  Themida, UPX, Enigma, …), an entry point outside executable code, the
  VMProtect `push imm32; ret` thunk, missing or tiny import tables, and the
  Valorant encrypted-globals magic. Findings add up to a 0–100 score and a
  verdict, so an agent can decide whether a devirtualizer is worth starting.
- **Handoff.** Dumps the module with the live base and rebuilt imports, then
  writes one folder of files: the dump, `<module>_functions.json` (tool-neutral
  addresses, RVAs, sizes, names, sections, findings), `<module>_offsets.hpp`,
  IDA/Ghidra/radare2 import scripts, a Triton lifter, SuperGhidra commands and a
  `<module>_handoff.md` with
  the exact NoVmp and vmp-lazy-unpack command lines.
- **Offsets only.** Any single format can be exported without the dump.

The heavy engines stay external, which is deliberate:

| Tool | Role |
| --- | --- |
| [NoVmp](https://github.com/can1357/NoVmp) | static VMProtect x64 3.x devirtualizer; run `NoVmp.exe <dump> -base <image base>`, add `-vms` for specific VMEnter RVAs |
| [vmp-lazy-unpack](https://github.com/x86rc/vmp-lazy-unpack) | VMProtect 3.x unpacker; run it on the original on-disk binary when the image is still packed |
| [VTIL-Core](https://github.com/vtil-project/VTIL-Core) / [VTIL2](https://github.com/pop-rip/vtil2) | optimize or recompile the VTIL NoVmp emits |
| [Triton](https://github.com/JonathanSalwan/Triton) | symbolic execution and lifting with the generated script |
| [VMProtect-devirtualization](https://github.com/JonathanSalwan/VMProtect-devirtualization) | research devirtualizer for VMProtect 2.x |
| [SuperGhidra](https://github.com/yuatemycat/SuperGhidra) | RTTI/MFC recovery, compilable C rewriting and a Ghidra MCP daemon |
| [ida-nexus](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-nexus), [ida-mcp](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-mcp), [radare2-mcp](https://github.com/radareorg/radare2-mcp) | point an agent at the imported database |

Echo gives these tools a clean, correctly based image and function list; it does
not pretend to devirtualize. A dump of an already-running protected game is
usually unpacked in memory, but static devirtualization still needs the VM entry
points from the original binary.

A handoff JSON can also be imported after a scan to apply matching function names to the current disassembly session by RVA. Module name and image size are checked, but do not uniquely identify a build.

### Unity (IL2CPP)

`GameAssembly` keeps a pointer to the loaded `global-metadata.dat`, so the
metadata is read from memory — already decrypted for games that ship it encrypted
on disk. Types, methods and fields are indexed by name, and the panel exports the
in-memory metadata plus a `GameAssembly.dll` dump for
[Il2CppDumper](https://github.com/Perfare/Il2CppDumper) or Cpp2IL. Offsets and
method addresses come from those tools; echo-reverse gives them a clean input.

### Source 2

Walks `CreateInterface` registries (`InterfaceReg` chains found through the
rip-relative `mov` in `CreateInterface`) and the schema classes the schema
compiler emits statically into each module, then exports a cs2-dumper-style
offsets header. Built for CS2, Dota 2 and Deadlock.

### Signature Doctor and RTTI

Signature Doctor takes a JSON catalog (signature, RVA and pointer entries), resolves
each row against the live process, and shows its resolution steps. Optional
`rel32` (byte offset to a signed 32-bit displacement), `addend`, `alignment`,
`readable` (1–4096 bytes), `moduleOnly`, and `valueCheck` (integer `width`, optional `signed`, `min` and `max` strings) checks refine each result. Pointer
chains use `offsets` (at most 32 steps). Set a baseline to compare RVAs across
module relocation; approve successful rows individually before exporting a JSON
manifest. Catalogs and baselines are local to the browser; baseline comparisons ignore JSON whitespace.
Signature Doctor's versioned catalog format is supported, including relative
references, pointer sizes, `readable`, `bytes`, `range`, `in_module` and
`alignment` checks. RTTI takes a list of object addresses and resolves the MSVC
class name for each in one batch.

### Scripts

An AngelScript editor with live diagnostics: a vendored copy of
[echo-angelscript-lsp](https://github.com/speedsunderscore/echo-angelscript-lsp)
(parser, analyzer, scope and type checker, and the Echo API declarations for
math, containers, drawing, memory, networking, threading, filesystem and the
engine SDKs) is compiled into the frontend, so unknown names and type errors
appear as you type with jump-to-line. Project folders and multiple `.as` files can be edited; the outline and completion include user symbols. Select an entry file to bundle its includes, or bundle all files. Check Project maps diagnostics from the bundle back to original files. The editor keeps a local recovery copy of the session. The API browser searches bundled declarations, and the test checklist explains how to validate compilation in Echo itself. Files can be
bundled in [as_bundler](https://github.com/sinistercodes/as_bundler) format, and
installing writes to `%APPDATA%\scripts`. Optional preprocessing expands
object-like defines, `__BUILD_*` timestamps and `STRHASH` / `STRHASH64` before
bundling. A committed API snapshot is checked against the live Echo docs in CI,
so the bundled LSP declarations track the current namespace, Unity and atomic
APIs instead of silently accepting an older host surface.

## MCP for agents

Endpoint: `POST http://127.0.0.1:9000/mcp`, MCP `2025-06-18`, JSON responses
(no SSE). The tool list combines relay tools with tools registered by the open workspace; use `tools/list` for the current set.

**Echo verbs** — served by the relay, straight through to the agents:

| Tool | Needs | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ping` | agent | whether Echo is attached, with pid and base |
| `modules` | agent | loaded modules: name, base, size |
| `read`, `read_batch` | agent | memory as hex, up to 1 MiB per read, 64 KiB per batch item |
| `sig_scan` | agent | IDA-style pattern scan (`48 8B 05 ? ? ? ?`) |
| `string_scan` | agent | literal string search in a module |
| `resolve_relative` | agent | resolve a rip-relative operand |
| `rtti_resolve` | agent | MSVC class name of the object at an address |
| `enumerate_functions` | agent | functions from the exception directory |
| `disassemble` | agent | Zydis listing, `size 0` stops at the function end |
| `disassemble_detail` | ext | Zydis instruction and operand details, up to 4 KiB |
| `attach`, `detach` | ext | attach by process name/PID or detach the current target |
| `process_alive` | ext | check target liveness without triggering an attachment |
| `query_region` | ext | query the mapping and permissions at an address |
| `resolve_export` | ext | resolve a named export in a loaded module |
| `write` | ext | hex bytes into target memory |
| `regions` | ext | mapped regions with synthesized `PAGE_*` protection |
| `exports`, `imports`, `iat_rebuild`, `sections`, `pe_header`, `pe_dirs`, `resource_tree` | ext | live PE tables for any loaded module |
| `dump` | ext | ask Echo to write a module dump in its scripts/dmp folder |
| `raw_scan`, `scan_grouped` | ext | bounded pattern search and neighboring values around scan hits |
| `scan_new`, `scan_filter` | ext | first pass and narrowing |
| `emulate` | ext | Unicorn run with registers, count, timeout, trace limit |
| `list_features`, `get_feature`, `set_feature` | menu lane | read and set overlay menu controls |

**App tools** — registered by the window over `ws /agent-app`, so agents reach
everything the UI can do:

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | relay lanes, attached process, loaded image — start here |
| `pe_info` | headers, sections, imports, exports of the main module |
| `list_functions` | functions with names from exports and UI renames, filterable |
| `disassemble_function` | the function containing an address, targets named |
| `function_stats`, `function_calls`, `search_operands` | size statistics, call sites and regex instruction search |
| `strings` | ASCII/UTF-16 strings from live memory, filterable |
| `read_value`, `write_value` | typed reads and writes: i8…f64, ptr, utf8, utf16, bytes |
| `pointer_chain` | `module + offsets[0]`, deref, `+ offsets[1]`, … |
| `snapshot_capture`, `snapshot_list`, `snapshot_compare`, `snapshot_delete` | persist and compare bounded memory snapshots |
| `runtime_capture_export` | export up to 16 MiB of live memory as JSON, with unreadable pages represented as gaps |
| `pointer_discover`, `pointer_revalidate` | bounded pointer-chain search and module-relative revalidation |
| `module_capture`, `module_captures`, `module_compare` | capture and compare module tables and samples |
| `value_scan_compare` | compare two MCP scan sessions by address |
| `script_api_search` | search the bundled Echo API declarations |
| `list_data_types`, `read_data_structure`, `export_data_types` | reusable nested structs/enums, live typed reads and JSON/C++ exports |
| `make_signature` | shortest unique IDA signature, rel32 and rip displacements wildcarded, verified |
| `xrefs_to` | branches, rip-relative loads and stored pointers, with their function |
| `value_scan` | Cheat-Engine-style first pass and narrowing |
| `value_scan_session`, `value_scan_status`, `value_scan_cancel` | independent incremental scans, progress and cancellation |
| `watch`, `watch_wait` | the UI watchlist; `watch_wait` blocks until a value changes |
| `emulate_function` | Unicorn run with stub and store logging |
| `dump_module` | module as a PE for the static tools |
| `unreal_index`, `unreal_find`, `unreal_dump`, `unreal_export_sdk` | the Unreal pipeline, including encrypted (Valorant) GObjects |
| `unity_index`, `unity_find`, `unity_export` | the IL2CPP pipeline |
| `source2_scan`, `source2_class`, `source2_export` | the Source 2 pipeline |
| `overlay_build`, `overlay_install` | generate or install the ESP overlay script from an entity layout |
| `deobf_scan`, `deobf_handoff`, `export_offsets` | triage the module and write the static-tool bundle or one offsets file |
| `script_check`, `script_template`, `script_install`, `script_list` | AngelScript validation, the relay and echo-ai-toolkit templates, install |
| `goto`, `show` | drive the window, so the user sees what the agent is looking at |

`goto`/`show` matter in practice: an agent can navigate the UI to the function it
is describing instead of only returning text.

Tool descriptions are detailed, and `status` reports each lane, so an agent can
tell "ext is not loaded" from "Echo is not attached".

## Build from source

The frontend is a plain Vite + React app; the relay is a Rust crate in
`app/src-tauri`.

Every push to `main` also publishes a `.deb` (and setup.exe) to the rolling
[`preview`](https://github.com/NetVar1337/echo-reverse/releases/tag/preview)
prerelease, for previewing the UI on Ubuntu 22.04 or newer (Echo itself still
needs Windows). Linux builds keep scripts in `~/.config/scripts`:

```sh
gh release download preview -R NetVar1337/echo-reverse -p '*.deb' --clobber
sudo apt install ./echo-reverse-preview_amd64.deb
```

Releases: push a `vX.Y.Z` tag. CI sets that version, signs the setup.exe and
.deb with the `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` repository secret, and publishes them
with the `latest.json` the in-app updater reads.

```powershell
cd app
npm install
npm run tauri dev      # desktop shell with the relay
```

Production build:

```powershell
cd app
npm run build                       # tsc --noEmit && vite build
npm run tauri build -- --no-bundle  # src-tauri/target/release/echo-reverse.exe
```

The standalone build embeds the web assets in the executable; WebView2 remains a platform requirement. The release workflow builds and publishes the standalone executable for version tags.

A plain browser against an existing relay (web-mv's, or the desktop app's):

```powershell
cd app
npm run dev            # http://localhost:1420
```

### Tests

```powershell
cd app
npm test               # test:echo + AngelScript/API conformance, what CI runs
npm run test:echo      # scanner sessions, memory tools, RPC mapping, PE, engines and generators
npm run check:as       # app/echo/**/*.as against the Echo API declarations
npm run check:api      # bundled declarations against the committed live-docs snapshot
npm run check:api:refresh # fetch llms-full.txt and refresh that snapshot
npm run typecheck
cd src-tauri
cargo test             # relay routing, MCP dispatch, timeouts
```

The suite runs against fake relays serving synthetic images, so it needs no game
and no Echo.

## Data on disk

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `%APPDATA%\scripts` | where Echo loads AngelScript from; install target |
| `%APPDATA%\echo-reverse\out` | module dumps, SDK headers, metadata exports |
| `localStorage["echo-relay-url"]` | relay URL set in Settings |

## What Echo does not expose

These were reverse-slop features and are gone because there is no Echo primitive
for them. They report "not available on the Echo backend" rather than failing
silently:

- the live debugger (breakpoints, stepping, call stacks, watchpoints)
- Frida instrumentation
- .NET/CLI metadata (the `.NET` tab only appears when a backend reports managed
  types)
- static file loading — the analysed image is always the attached main module
- a background analysis pass: the Analysis tab works from live function and
  instruction data, but Echo does not expose a progress stream for one
- process enumeration: Echo exposes the target that is already attached; the
  extension can attach by name/PID, but cannot list every Windows process
- the kernel bridge, WFP network capture and the HTTP proxy
- Lua scripting and the C++ MCP server

Devirtualization and lifting are not Echo primitives either. Those stay with
NoVmp, VTIL, Triton and vmp-lazy-unpack; echo-reverse prepares their input and
writes the handoff scripts (see
[Deobfuscation and handoff](#deobfuscation-and-handoff)).

## Troubleshooting

**Relay unreachable.** The app hosts it on port 9000; check nothing else holds
that port (`netstat -ano | findstr 9000`). If another relay is there, the UI uses
it — point Echo's agent at that port instead, or set `ECHO_RELAY_PORT`.

**Agent connects but panels stay empty.** Echo is not attached, or the script
failed. `GET http://127.0.0.1:9000/status` shows which lanes are live; a missing
`core` means `echo-reverse.as` is not loaded, or its `open_socket` failed — press
**Connect** on its tab in Echo.

**Writes, scans and the emulator are refused.** Those need
`echo-reverse.as` on `/agent-ext`. Reads do not.

**Script install fails.** It needs the desktop shell (a browser tab downloads the
file instead) and a plain file name ending in `.as`. Echo still has to load it
from its own menu; reopening that menu is what refreshes the list.

**Dump won't open in IDA/Ghidra.** Dumps keep the live base and virtual layout,
so load them at the reported image base with "manual load" if the loader
complains, and expect resolved pointers instead of named imports.

**Emulation stops immediately.** Calls out of the module are stubbed, not
followed. Pass initial registers and a `count`/`timeout_us`, and check the trace
for the first missing stub.

## Security notes

- The relay binds loopback only and checks `Host`/`Origin`; it has no
  authentication of its own. Anything on the machine that can reach port 9000 can
  call the same tools the UI can, including `write` and `emulate` when the ext
  agent is loaded.
- App tools run inside the window: closing the app drops `/agent-app` and the
  app tools disappear from `tools/list`.
- MCP clients inherit full read/write access to the attached process. Point them
  at a test account, not a live one.
- Scripts installed to `%APPDATA%\scripts` run inside Echo with Echo's privileges.
  Read a script before loading it.
